title: Measure the paired work events and the identity they carry
question: At this head, does either end of the five paired profiler work events pass a component identity, and does the page agent`s microtask-delimited frame hold both ends of a pair?

commands.teardown: node .commandcode/skills/control-ai-browsers/scripts/control.mjs down chrome-beta-gemma4; node .commandcode/skills/control-angular-dev-app/scripts/control.mjs down --target counter

pairs.question: Which ProfilerEvent values does each installed @angular/core declare, and which of them are a start and an end that bracket one unit of work?

reader.how: one reader applied to each installed package: find `var ProfilerEvent;`, take the block up to `})(ProfilerEvent ||`, read every `ProfilerEvent[ProfilerEvent["Name"] = N] = "Name";` assignment, then look the five pair names up in that derived list by name and take their numbers from it
reader.why: the enum is a runtime IIFE in the shipped chunk, so the names and numbers are read from what the browser would execute, and the pair numbers are derived from that list rather than quoted

sources.package: panel: the @angular/core the extension panel builds against
fixture: the @angular/core the counter page loads

pairs.finding: Both installed builds declare the same 26 values, and the five pairs are 2/3, 4/5, 12/13, 18/19 and 24/25 of that derived list.

identity.question: What does each emission site of the five pairs pass, and does that argument list carry a component identity?

reader.how: one reader over the chunk the page loads: every `profiler(` call site with its 1-indexed line, the call text, the argument list as written, and — where the first argument is a local constant — that constant`s own `const x = a ? ProfilerEvent.A : ProfilerEvent.B;` line, resolved by scanning upward at most eight lines
reader.pattern: a line containing `profiler(` that is neither `const profiler = function (event, instance = null, eventFn)` nor `function setProfiler(`, split on top-level commas
reader.why: the enum number says an event exists; only the call site says what it carries, and SC3 turns on whether a bracket names a component. The reader names the call site and the argument list it read; it does not infer an argument from a neighbouring call

namedAbsence.evidence: the profiler brackets change detection and names nothing: the start is `profiler(ProfilerEvent.ChangeDetectionStart)` and each end is `profiler(ProfilerEvent.ChangeDetectionEnd)`, so the callback receives the parameter default `instance = null` with no `eventFn`, and measured on both pages all 3 starts and all 3 ends carried a null instance and an undefined eventFn
namedAbsence.consequence: SC3`s cannot-tell is the answer for a ChangeDetection interval: the profiler brackets the frame`s change detection and names nothing. The identity that does exist for a Component bracket arrives on its end (`componentView[CONTEXT]`) and never on its start, so a ComponentStart with no end in the frame is unnamed and must report the same absence

identity.finding: Three pairs carry an identity on both ends (TemplateUpdate, LifecycleHook, HostBindingsUpdate), one carries it on its end only (Component), and one carries none at all (ChangeDetection).

frames.question: Are both emission sites of a pair inside one bracketed call, and does the page agent`s microtask-delimited frame hold both ends?

agentFrame.how: the agent opens its cycle on the first TemplateUpdateStart of a task and closes it from a queued microtask, so the cycle spans the rest of that task`s synchronous work and nothing after it

disagreements.label: Component
disagreements.detail: each start and its end are in one try/finally (renderComponent 5740/5744, detectChangesInComponent 6166/6171), but the outermost ComponentStart of a task precedes the first TemplateUpdateStart that opens the frame: 3 of 6 starts on / and 3 of 9 on /field-form arrived with no frame open, and only the inner brackets share a frame
disagreements.narratorObeys: a Component start recorded with no frame open belongs to the frame the task opens later, or the interval is unmeasured; it is never paired with an end from another frame

frames.rule: The agent frame is not the profiler bracket. A start and its end must be matched by recorded arrival order and the measured nesting — a pair`s end is emitted inside the same synchronous call as its start — and a start that arrives with no frame open belongs to the frame the same task opens later or is reported unmeasured. A duration is never taken from the agent`s cycle alone.
frames.finding: Both ends of all five pairs sit in one synchronous call except ChangeDetection, whose start and end are emitted in two different calls; the agent`s frame holds both ends for TemplateUpdate, LifecycleHook and HostBindingsUpdate, only the inner brackets for Component, and never for ChangeDetection.

negatives: HostBindingsUpdate 24/25 fired zero times on / across three ticks, so the counter page cannot witness that pair; it was measured on /field-form instead, where the FormRoot directive carries host bindings
the three ticks on each page produced the same event order, so the frame orders recorded here are one observed order repeated, not a distribution

portalAttempt.target: the pinned zoneful Insurance Portal worktree, the repository`s verification target
portalAttempt.lacks: a zoneless profiler stream at a supported version: the pinned worktree is Angular 20.3.35 zone-backed, and extension/agent-main.js:500-542 refuses a page older than 22.1.3 and refuses a zoneful page before it ever calls setProfiler

witness.instrumentation: one profiler callback per page on a tab the `run` command closes; the extension keeps its single setProfiler subscription and no page gained a global, an append-only list or a second tap

doesNotSettle: whether a component whose work the profiler bracketed can be named from anything other than the ComponentEnd instance: no site passes a name, and the watcher`s own name is not the profiler`s
what a production build emits: every site read here is in the development bundle the fixture serves, and the agent already refuses a page without ng.ɵsetProfiler
how often a bracket arrives with no matching end: the witness drove three ticks per page and every start it saw was matched, so the unmatched case is T003`s fixture, not this measurement
whether the emission sites move between point releases: this record cites the two versions this head installs (panel 22.1.8, fixture 22.2.2) and the suite re-derives them on every run
what the portal page emits: the pinned zoneful worktree was named and refused, not driven, because the agent refuses it before subscribing
